ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Low-flow injury despite preserved oxygenation

A patient develops profound hypotension after a large myocardial infarction. Arterial oxygen saturation remains 98% with oxygen supplementation, yet urine output falls and lactate rises. Which additional consequence of reduced perfusion makes ischemia more damaging than isolated oxygen deprivation?

  1. Reduced nutrient delivery and impaired metabolite clearance
  2. Increased delivery of glucose to hypoxic cells
  3. Accelerated removal of hydrogen ions
  4. Selective blockade of oxygen binding to hemoglobin
  5. Increased mitochondrial ATP synthesis
Answer and explanation

Reduced nutrient delivery and impaired metabolite clearance

Low blood flow restricts glucose delivery and removal of acidic metabolites as well as oxygen delivery.

Option explanations

Reduced nutrient delivery and impaired metabolite clearance: Low blood flow restricts glucose delivery and removal of acidic metabolites as well as oxygen delivery.

Increased delivery of glucose to hypoxic cells: Reduced perfusion decreases nutrient delivery.

Accelerated removal of hydrogen ions: Poor perfusion impairs acid clearance.

Selective blockade of oxygen binding to hemoglobin: Ischemia is a blood-flow problem, not a selective hemoglobin-binding defect.

Increased mitochondrial ATP synthesis: Insufficient oxygen and substrate reduce ATP production.
